changes: Chickahominy Indian Tribe and Chickahominy Indian Tribe - Eastern Division receive separate profiles with eight concise facts, four titled historical/context layers and four direct own-publisher resources.
Chickahominy history covers river homelands, displacement, education barriers and community persistence. Its published environmental vision remains an aspiration, not a measured outcome.

Eastern Division history connects its school, formation of a distinct government and incorporation without treating twentieth-century institutional dates as the beginning of the people. Its Tribal Government remains distinct from the separate CIED nonprofit.

CIT-ED food-sovereignty material describes a 2022 gardening and composting account and 2025 garden/food-forest plans. Completion, current availability and independent environmental outcomes are not established.

Each of four source-directory rows receives a separate identity link: one Virginia and one federal record per profile. The two governments are never merged under a generic Chickahominy alias. Dated federal source editions remain unchanged.

Explore This Record adds native links to Lands and Facts And Sources, with Context And Resources only when public context exists. These links are intended to shorten reading journeys without hiding substantive content or requiring JavaScript. Final browser verification is recorded separately.
The selective canonical overlay preserves all 461 previous profile objects and every prior fact clock. Existing fact holds and pending publisher-reuse reviews remain unchanged.
